(Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good afternoon everyone, it’s time to dive back into the mailbag and answer some of your questions. Remember to send in your questions for our bi-weekly call by e-mail to pinstripealleyblog [at] gmail [dot] com . Darth_Lazarus asks: If the CBA negotiations go really sideways is there a possibility we see replacement player games next year? Never say never, but I doubt the owners would want to go this route even if it’s looking like the season is completely lost. Recruiting scab players at this point in the league’s history would be a black eye on ownership and would completely kill any goodwill they could have with the public as these negotiations drag on, as the product on the field will be a clearly inferior copy that wouldn’t draw much interest while also making them look desperate to recoup on the broadcast deals they’ve negotiated. Speaking of those broadcasting rights, while the league is a much more regional product than the NFL or NBA and several teams were having trouble finding an actual partner for their TV audience, it’s my hope that the prospect of future negotiations with broadcasters is one of the pressure points pushing ownership to get to the table sooner rather than later resulting in an actual season being played out in 2027 — perhaps a bit too hopeful, considering the lines in the sand that have been drawn this time around, but a girl can dream. Johnny1944 asks: It seems JD was overhyped for years by Cash. Does he have any real value? Jasson Domínguez’s career is looking like a relatively unremarkable one, which is what tends to happen to the majority of MLB players — but most players don’t get compared to Mickey Mantle when they were 17 years old. That unfair expectation has felt like a weight on Domínguez’s shoulders the entire time that he’s been in the organization, with every glimpse of a solid run down in the minors being heralded as the turning point where he was going to spark a path straight to the majors. However, Domínguez has now had two full seasons in proximity to the majors, and while he’s still very young entering his age-24 season in 2027 it just doesn’t seem like there’s much to work with in his game. Our own Andrés tackled the idea of whether the Yankees should move on from Domínguez the other day, and while his conclusion was that there’s no pressure to do so immediately time is running out for the former wonder prospect. He’s got one minor league option remaining meaning he’s likely to start the year in the minors, and while there’s some underlying promise in his peripherals the majority of his Savant page is disappointing. Domínguez’s defense has been atrocious to watch, and he’s alternated from being unable to hit lefties to being unable to hit righties. If there was just some consistency to his game he’d at least be able to stick around as a bench option in the majors, but as is he’s got to get consistent playing time to try and make something of himself and he isn’t going to find that in pinstripes at the moment. OLDY MOLDY asks: How reliable are Cole, Fried, and Rodón next year considering recent arm problems in the last 3 seasons and age? Any innings projections? Does Schlittler come back to earth in 2027? I don’t have many concerns about Max Fried at the moment — he’ll probably be good for one short-term IL stint but otherwise give the team 25-30 starts and has been lights out when he has been active. Likewise, while Gerrit Cole has missed significant time over the past couple of seasons the core issue has now been dealt with and he should be fully healthy entering 2027. It’s wild to think that we’re already seven years into the nine-year deal that Cole signed with the team, but there’s just two seasons left of his contract and if you told me back then that he’d have compiled three top five Cy Young finishes with one win up to this point, I’d be pretty content entering the final days of that deal. Carlos Rodón has salvaged his Yankees career quite well following his disastrous first year in pinstripes, but of the three his health still concerns me more going forward — not enough to panic, but enough to keep my eye on how he’s getting through each start even when he’s on. As for Cam Schlittler, the sky is the ceiling for the team’s newfound ace and while it would certainly be unrealistic to expect a 1.95 ERA as the standard going forward I think he’ll remain the team’s best pitcher next year as he comes into his own.

item.title: Uli Hoeneß claps back on criticism of Jonas Urbig
item.description: Bayern Munich's board member and former president Uli Hoeness drinks beer as he attends the Oktoberfest beer festival in Munich, southern Germany, on September 20, 2026. The world's biggest beer festival Oktoberfest runs until October 4, 2026. (Photo by Tobias SCHWARZ / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Jonas Urbig has not yet become the number one at Bayern Munich this season, but he has been accumulating a great track record of performances so far. However, not everyone is convinced of Urbig, despite being trusted for both Bayern Munich and, recently, the German national team. Uli Hoeneß was recently asked whethe r he is convinced Jonas Urbig is capable of becoming Bayern’s number one, leading to quite an exchange between himself and the journalist. “I have absolutely no doubt about it. It’s a very smart decision. Jonas Urbig will get this opportunity. Everyone at FC Bayern is prepared for that. Based on his performance on the pitch and his character, he deserves this chance. Then we’ll see what happens next. He has the ability to make it,” Hoeneß told Welt am Sonntag , as captured by @iMiaSa nMia . “Urbig has never been the number one at a world-class club; Neuer’s shoes to fill would be enormous,” the interviewer said. “So should we spend €50 million on a goalkeeper just because he’s played a few Champions Leag ue games and a few know-it-alls are demanding that? Absolutely not,” Hoeneß responded. It is a perfect response to the journalist in what is truly a ridiculous counterpoint. Without taking a shot at young talent, clubs would be forced to always spend big money on proven talent elsewhere, which would not be financially feasib le. Urbig seems up for the challenge and, while there are no guarantees, he is without a doubt the best option at the moment. Join the conversation! PJ Woodland vs. Ryan Coleman-Williams As he has all year, Woodland is likely to draw the role of guarding the opposing team’s best wide receiver. In this case, it’s Coleman-Williams. Along with 5 more touchdowns on the ground, he presents the same sort of threat as LSU has seen as recently has Byrum Brown. The body type is different, but the danger is the same. TJ Dottery and Dahvon Keys on the second level will be important for when Russell wants to leave the pocket. Ty Benefield can also be thrown in to that group, especially considering what we’ve seen him do as a spy this year. While you feel really good about LSU’s ability to pressure Russell with their 4-man rush, how the Tigers are able to limit him from the second level is equally important.

item.description: James Maclennan-Imagn Images LPGA star Nelly Korda on track for historic feat after winning Player of the Year appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LPGA superstar Nelly Korda had an impressive 2026 to say the least. The 28-year-old began the year with a victory at the Tournament of Champions. She ended up winning two majors this year as well, earning victories at the Chevron Championship and US Women’s Open . Korda was recently announced as the Rolex Player of the Year following her strong season. The World No. 1 player is also nearing a place in the Hall of Fame. She is one point shy of reaching Hall of Fame status. Korda still has time in 2026 to accomplish the feat. If she cannot do it this year, Korda is still on track to reach the Hall of Fame at some point in the near future. Korda’s accomplishments at only 28 years old are extraordinary. She’s already won four majors and two Player of the Year Awards. It’s easy to forget that she’s only been a professional golfer for 10 years now, yet Korda is already establishing herself as an all-time great. Korda will look to reach Hall of Fame status soon while maintaining her position as the No. 1 player in the world. Jeeno Thitkul has 428 total points and is only one point behind Korda’s 429. item.description: Everton striker continues scoring streak with PL double 📈 It's been an up-and-down campaign so far for Everton's Thierno Barry. The Toffees striker has had plenty of goalscoring opportunities in 2026/27 and came into Friday's match against Coventry with one of the highest individual xG rates in the Premier League, but only four goals to show. However, it appears as though the 24-year-old has turned a corner with a quickfire second-half brace against Coventry. Everton initially trailed after Yann Gboho's struck first and Barry's towering header levelled the score. Just five minutes later, Barry added his second of the evening, and his fourth goal in just three matches in all competitions with another close-range header. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Chris Tanev and Dakota Joshua returned this past week, but the Toronto Maple Leafs still have another couple of key players who’ve been out for a while. On Friday, there’s good news on John Tavares , but not so good news on Kirill Marchenko . With the latter, Marchenko went down with a lower-body injury on October 26 during a game in Calgary against the Flames. item.title: Milan target defensive reinforcements with Inácio top of the list
item.description: Milan target defensive reinforcements with Inácio top of the list Milan are preparing to strengthen their defence when the transfer window opens in January, and Sporting CP captain Gonçalo Inácio remains their first choice. According to TuttoMercatoWeb , the Rossoneri see a new centre-back as a priority with less than two months until the market reopens. Inácio is still top of the list, but a deal will be difficult because of Sporting’s high valuation. Milan will try anyway, hoping the Portuguese club can be persuaded to negotiate. ITALY – NOVEMBER 05: Ruben Amorim looks on before the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match at Stadio San Siro on November 05, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Milan’s January defensive targets The 25-year-old knows Ruben Amorim well, having played under the Milan coach for several seasons at Sporting. He reportedly has a €60m release clause, although Portuguese outlet A Bola suggest a fee of €40-45m could be enough to sign him. Inácio isn’t the only name on the list. Milan are also considering investing in younger players, and they are big admirers of Borussia Dortmund’s Luca Reggiani . The 2008-born Italian left Sassuolo’s academy for Germany at 16 and made his Bundesliga and Champions League debuts last season. Union Saint-Gilloise’s Massiré Sylla is another option. The 21-year-old Senegalese defender joined the Belgian club from Norwegian side Lyn in January, after being named Young Player of the Year in Norway’s second tier.

Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After the Portland Blazers parted ways with head coach Tiago Splitter in favor of Micah Nori, many wondered how it would affect the team’s young players, including fourth-year guard Scoot Henderson . Coach Nori’s unique approach to his first year with the Blazers included instructing his coaching staff to read “The Old Man and the Sea,” by Ernest Hemingway. For the players, it’s Nori’s attention to detail that stands out most, Henderson said, per The Athletic’s Jason Quick. “We lacked small details,” Henderson said. “Great teams are big on that, from what I can see, just playing against them. Going back to last year, we lacked some of the small details. Nori is helping us with that.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Scoot Henderson and the Blazers have the best record (6-1) in the Western Conference standings. Two weeks into the regular season, head coach Micah Nori has his team fully committed to success, led by All-Star Deni Avdija and veterans Damian Lillard, Ja Morant, and Jrue Holiday. “I’m getting way too much credit, I really am; I’m not just saying that,” Nori said. “I’m not trying to be overly humble, but I’m getting way too much credit for putting really good players in good positions. It’s playing to their strengths; that’s all.” Portland is leading the league in scoring (121.9). Last year, the Blazers averaged the most turnovers in the NBA, more than 17 a game. This season, they rank 14th out of 30, averaging nearly two fewer. The vast improvements, along with early returns this season, have them positioned to become one of the better teams in the association. Their schedule hasn’t been easy either, with wins over the Los Angeles Lakers, Denver Nuggets, and Phoenix Suns, including a 132-119 victory over the Suns on Wednesday. Damian Lillard has been solid since returning from his Achilles injury, averaging 20.1 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 4.1 assists, although his 31.7% shooting from three still needs some work. Deni Avdija has been even better, putting up 23.4 points, 6.4 rebounds, and 6.4 assists on 47.8% from the field, being that primary playmaker who can run the offense without needing Lillard to set things up. Donovan Clingan has also been important as a rebounder and rim protector, giving Portland some much-needed size down low. The other surprise is that the Blazers have won three straight games without Ja Morant

item.title: Giants-Eagles final injury report: Cam Skattebo misses practice, doubtful for Sunday
item.description: Cam Skattebo missed a fourth straight practice on Friday due to his hamstring injury, but the New York Giants are not ruling their leading rusher out for Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Skattebo is officially considered doubtful. “Let’s see what happens” head coach John Harbaugh said of Skattebo’s status. Wide receiver Malik Nabers , who missed practice on Thursday, yelled to reporters that he practice on Friday . Harbaugh said that Nabers’ health is “not an issue” for Sunday. If Skattebo cannot play, Devin Singletary will be the Giants’ primary running back against the Eagles. Gregory Desrosiers is the other back on the 53-man roster, and Phil Mafah and Eric Gray are on the practice squad. The other injury of note for the Giants involves wide reciever/returner Charlie Jones . He turned up on the injury report this week with a hand injury, and is listed as questionable. “He’s managing it,” Harbaugh said. “He was out today catching and everything like that. Just want to make sure he could catch. I haven’t talked to him yet. We’ll see how he felt.” The Giants have an open roster spot after dropping quarterback Jake Haener from the 53-man roster on Thursday. Adding someone with running back, return experience, or both, might make sense before Sunday. item.title: Eagles legend upset at his former team for pushing Jeff Stoutland out: ‘Don’t give me this crap’
item.description: Former Eagles legend Jason Kelce is upset about the narrative that Eagles players wanted Jeff Stoutland gone after last season. On Tuesday , 97.5 The Fanatic radio host Bill Colarulo reported that Eagles players wanted a new offensive line coach to lead the room. They wanted a new voice. So, after 13 seasons, Stoutland left the Eagles’ organization in February. “That one very much upset me,” Kelce said on the 94WIP morning show about the Stoutland report. “Because the reason to move off of Jeff Stoutland had nothing to do with the players. Had to do with the building wanting to go in a different direction. That’s fine, but don’t give me this crap, trying to defer direction on the decisions you guys wanted to make.” Kelce is upset that certain members of the Eagles’ organization are not willing to stand behind their statements. They are hiding behind a report. “The leaks coming out and the unnamed sources,” Kelce said about what bothers him. “It really bothers me because as a player. And the reason I’m telling people listening, I would take anything you hear from an unnamed source with a giant grain of salt. Because ultimately that person isn’t willing to stand behind it in front of a camera, and usually that unnamed source has some type of incentive or reason that they’re putting this out to a media member. And it’s usually to cover their own behind.” For Sunday’s NFC East clash between the Eagles and the Giants, the over/under is set at 38.5 total points on Kalshi . item.title: Haaland’s Late Strike Seals City Comeback
item.description: Kyle Robertson/Columbus Dispatch, Kyle Robertson / USA TODAY NETWORK Manchester City found a way to win again thanks to a late goal from Erling Haaland. The striker netted the deciding score twelve minutes from time to secure a 3-2 victory over RB Leipzig in the Champions League. This result gets the team back on track after a tough loss to Brighton on Saturday. Haaland has now scored thirteen goals in just nine appearances against this German side, which is more than he has scored against any other opponent in his entire career. The match was not an easy night for the visitors as City led twice but had to fight hard for every point. Leipzig scored first after a mistake by Castello Lukeba turned the ball into his own net. Ridle Baku then put Leipzig ahead again in the second half with a smart finish from a tight angle. Enzo Fernandez restored the lead for City with a powerful header from an Iliman Ndiaye cross. The game stayed tight until Haaland tapped in a low pass from Elliot Anderson to win it. Haaland Knows How To Finish Erling Haaland proved once again that he is the man to have when the clock is ticking down. He had just three touches in the first half and looked like a bystander before the end. Yet he stepped up to score the winner when his team needed him most. Sky Sports reported that this goal marks his thirteenth against RB Leipzig. That number shows he has a special connection with this specific opponent that few other players can match. His ability to find the net in the final minutes gives his team a real edge in tight games. City Needs To Fix The Defense Even with a win, the defensive mistakes in this game are a worry for any fan. The team gifted the first goal to Leipzig because of a comical error by Castello Lukeba. Gianluigi Donnarumma made a great save early in the second half but got beaten seconds later by Ridle Baku. Baku tucked the ball in from a difficult angle, catching the goalkeeper out at his near post. These lapses in judgment cost City valuable time and energy they do not need to waste against top teams. Jeremy Doku came on to help spur the team into their best spell of the game. The introduction of fresh legs helped create the chance that led to the winning goal. Rayan Cherki also hit the woodwork for City while David Raum rattled the frame for Leipzig in the frantic finale. The game ended with a 3-2 score that reflects how much action both sides created.

item.title: ‘The best possible news’ – José Mourinho reveals his hopes for Atlético vs Barcelona
item.description: ‘The best possible news’ – José Mourinho reveals his hopes for Atlético vs Barcelona Real Madrid head coach José Mourinho has on Friday spoken out on the upcoming showdown between his side’s two main La Liga title challengers. The headline fixture of the upcoming gameweek in Spain’s top-flight is of course set to play out at the Metropolitano on Sunday evening. The matchup in question will see Diego Simeone’s Atlético Madrid play host to Barcelona, in a battle between 1st and 2nd in the table. Just three points separate the top three in La Liga heading into the clash, with Real Madrid sitting in 3rd. Speaking during an appearance in front of the media ahead of Los Blancos’ showdown with Valencia on Saturday, the aforementioned José Mourinho was therefore asked for his take on the upcoming Metropolitano matchup. And the Portuguese tactician went on to admit: ”Atlético vs Barcelona? I’d like both of them to lose! Unfortunately, that’s not possible. Points will inevitably be dropped, and that’s the best possible news.” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Everton Eye £44m Brazilian Forward: Is He Worth The Gamble?
item.description: Everton Eye £44m Brazilian Forward: Is He Worth The Gamble? Everton have settled into a stable rhythm under The Friedkin Group, whose ownership has brought stability off the pitch and carried the club into the new Hill Dickinson Stadium. On it, David Moyes has his side seventh in the Premier League as of November 6, helped by a 1–0 away win at Newcastle United and a place in the EFL Cup quarter-finals. Much of that progress rests heavily on one man. Thierno Barry, the 23-year-old French striker signed before the summer 2026 window, has started all nine league games and is the team’s top scorer with four Premier League goals and eight in all competitions. He holds a secure contract and works as a classic target man, pinning centre-backs and giving Moyes an indispensable focal point up front. Behind Barry, the central cover is thin. Academy product Braiden Graham is the only other central option of note, and the club signed no major centre-forward over the summer, focusing on permanent midfield and wing additions while losing Iliman Ndiaye. Barry therefore has no senior, high-quality alternative to rotate with or to stretch defences when Moyes’ rigid system needs a different kind of threat, so the club needs reinforcement before the 2027 windows. Sport Witness links the Toffees with a 2027 move for Palmeiras striker Vitor Roque, reporting high interest despite competition from Chelsea, Tottenham and Manchester United . Palmeiras value the 21-year-old Brazilian at €50 million (£44million). Roque is no conventional number nine. He thrives on explosive acceleration, pressing defenders and chasing direct balls into space from wide left channels. After scoring 20 goals in 2025, left ankle surgery cost him three months this year, and he has nine goals and one assist in 39 appearances (1,984 minutes) in 2026. His work rate suits Moyes’ defensive system, but Moyes wants a physically sturdy focal point, and any deal depends on Roque regaining his explosiveness. Should Everton spend £44 million on Vitor Roque? SAO PAULO, BRAZIL – NOVEMBER 05: Vitor Roque of Palmeiras celebrates after scoring his team’s fourth goal during the 2026 Brasileirao 34th-round match between Palmeiras and Remo at Nubank Parque on November 05, 2026 in Sao Paulo, Brazil. (Photo by Alexandre Schneider/Getty Images) No. The club should decline a move at that price and pursue a traditional, physical target man. The Friedkin Group has provided financial stability, but committing a fee among the club’s largest to a player who has spent much of 2026 regaining his pace carries an unacceptable level of risk. Moyes’ side sits seventh and relies on Barry’s physical presence to hold the ball up. Roque, an arrow who needs freedom to drift wide, clashes with Moyes’ positional discipline and dislike of forwards abandoning the central box. Spending £44million on that luxury alternative would misallocate capital, because he cannot easily deputise as a lone central reference if Barry suffers an injury.

item.title: Knicks rush to Taylor Swift’s defense after Tyler Kolek’s ‘fakest fan’ callout
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images. Knicks rush to Taylor Swift’s defense after Tyler Kolek’s ‘fakest fan’ callout appeared first on ClutchPoints . After being called out by New York Knicks star Tyler Kolek for being the team’s “fakest celebrity fan,” the organization has defended Taylor Swift , who attended Game 4 of the NBA Finals. The Knicks issued a statement, defending Swift’s longtime fandom and her “long history with Madison Square Garden.” They are grateful for her support. “Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization,” the statement read. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Knicks star Tyler Kolek ’s comments about Taylor Swift’s fandom Brad Penner-Imagn Images. Kolek and his teammate, Mile McBride, did a video for Deflected. They were asked who the “fakest celebrity fan” of the Knicks is: Kolek said there are several “performative” fans who clout-chase by going to games. Among those celebrities was Swift. “At the Knicks games, I would say it’s very performative ’cause they just want to be seen at the game; they’re not necessarily fans,” said Kolek. “Maybe Taylor Swift. I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games.” McBride knew Kolek might have made a mistake, saying, “Swifties not gonna like that answer,” before shouting out other celebrity fans like Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan. Kolek tried to save himself, conceding that Swift may have “a lot going on so she can’t come all the time.” Still, he finds it “a little performative.” Swift attended Game 4 of the NBA Finals when the Knicks played the San Antonio Spurs. They famously erased a 29-point deficit to gain a 3-1 lead in the series. She was decked out in a Knicks-themed shirt that read, “Stevie Knicks.” Swift sat alongside Mariska Hargitay and Este and Alana Haim. They stayed enthusiastic despite the Knicks trailing almost the entire game. However, a few weeks earlier, she attended one of the Knicks’ games against the Cleveland Cavaliers in the Eastern Conference Finals. She was with her husband and Ohio native Travis Kelce. item.title: Aaron Rodgers’ Brother Jordan Makes Unexpected Admission After Years of Family Tension: ‘I Trust the Guy’
item.description: Mega; FS2/FayesVision/WENN Aaron Rodgers is receiving public praise from his younger brother, Jordan Rodgers , following years of tension within their family. During an ESPN appearance on Wednesday, November 4, Jordan complimented the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback ‘s experience and ability to lead his team into the playoffs, according to an Entertainment Weekly article published on Friday, November 6. “This one might surprise you a little bit,” Jordan, 38, said before naming his brother as his pick for the most dependable quarterback, per the report. He explained that the Pittsburgh Steelers ‘ strong defense and running game allow Aaron to focus on managing the offense rather than carrying the entire team. “I just feel like I trust the guy that’s got the MVPs, that has the veteran status, that’s seen everything,” Jordan said. The comments come months after Aaron, 42, began reconnecting with relatives following a family rift that lasted more than a decade. In July, Aaron shared photos, via Instagram , with his parents, Ed Rodgers and Darla Rodgers , and older brother Luke Rodgers . Per the report, Jordan and his wife, JoJo Fletcher , were not pictured at the gathering but liked the post. TALA /MEGA As First for Sports previously reported , Aaron discussed repairing his family relationships during a September appearance on the Not Just Football podcast. “There were tough conversations for sure,” he admitted on the podcast, adding that he was in a “much better headspace.” The quarterback also credited his wife, Brittani — whose identity has not been shared publicly — for supporting him through the reconciliation, during the podcast appearance. However, according to Page Six , a source said Jordan’s relationship with Aaron remains complicated. “It still seems like a very sensitive topic for Jordan,” the source said. According to Entertainment Weekly , the brothers’ strained relationship became public in 2016 when Jordan discussed their lack of contact while competing for Fletcher’s heart on season 12 of ABC’s reality dating show The Bachelorette . Aaron and the Steelers currently lead the AFC North with a 6-2 record and are riding a four-game winning streak as they prepare to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, November 15, per the team’s official website . item.title: Giants trade Reiver Sanmartin for Robert Cranz
item.description: HARRISBURG, PA - AUGUST 25: Robert Cranz #46 of the Harrisburg Senators pitches during the game between the Chesapeake Baysox and the Harrisburg Senators at FNB Field on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kyle Mace/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) The San Francisco Giants announced a small deal on Friday, as a trickle down from Monday’s roster-cutting actions. Lefty reliever Reiver Sanmartin has been traded to the Washington Nationals in exchange for Minor League reliever Robert Cranz. It’s not news that Sanmartin is gone, as the Giants announced that he had been designated for assignment on Monday, amongst the flurry of moves that got the roster back down to 40 players at the deadline. But most DFA’d players leave with nothing in return, so it’s nice that Sanmartin was an exception, and the Giants were able to get something back to allow the Nationals to jump to the front of the line. As is always the case with these sorts of deals, it’s not a huge haul they got back, but Cranz is interesting. The 23-year old right-hander was drafted in the seventh round of the 2024 draft (pick No. 200 on the dot) out of Oklahoma State, and received a mildly underslot bonus of $190,000. He performed fairly well in Low-A and High-A in his first full season in 2025, and started to make a name for himself in 2026. Cranz opened the year in High-A, where he had a 2.25 ERA and a 2.68 FIP, with a whopping 27 strikeouts in just 16 innings. He kept it up in AA, where he posted a 3.42 ERA and a 2.95 FIP, with 40 strikeouts in 26.1 innings. A native of Keller, Texas, Cranz made it to AAA to end the year, and that’s where his success ended. It was a rude introduction to the top ring of the Minors, and he ended his cup of coffee there with a 13.11 ERA, a 7.17 FIP, and just nine strikeouts in 11.2 innings. Cranz mostly throws hard stuff, as in AAA he used his four-seam fastball (which averaged 95.2 mph) nearly half of the time, while throwing his cutter and slider more than 20% of the time each. There’s definitely something intriguing there, and he’ll be a big part of AAA Sacramento’s bullpen depth this year, and have a chance to play his way into the Majors.

item.title: Matthias Jaissle caught in the storm as Newcastle struggle without European fix
item.description: Panic building among fans as club visit Craven Cottage but head coach has resolute support of hierarchy At least Matthias Jaissle has a sense of humour. “There’s a lot of storm at the moment,” reflected Newcastle’s head coach on Thursday. A wry smile suggested he was not referring to the north-east weather. Jaissle has seen his tactics, team selection, man management and entire philosophy rubbished in recent days but, on current evidence, appears to be holding his nerve. After all, it is not Jaissle’s fault that his appointment has coincided with supporters, players and directors struggling to adjust to life without Champions League involvement. A disappointing 12th-place finish under Eddie Howe last season dictates that there are no more exciting trips to Barcelona, Paris and Marseille and, significantly, no much-needed boost to club finances. Indeed, Newcastle are finding life without last term’s continental fix so tricky that they travel to Fulham on Saturday with the disgruntled mindset of a passenger accustomed to flying business class who suddenly finds themselves stuck in a cramped, mid-row economy seat. item.title: Football Daily | You want proper football? Here are the FA Cup first-round ties to look out for
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. item.title: Nottingham Forest’s historic goal drought at home is part of longstanding problem
item.description: Oliver Glasner’s side are yet to score at City Ground this season but troubles in front of goal precede his arrival Nottingham Forest and Schalke are yet to score at home in 2026-27. The former are one of only five teams in the history of the English top flight to have failed to score in their first four home league matches. Three of the preceding four also drew a blank in game five, which will be deflating news for Oliver Glasner with Manchester City heading to the City Ground on Saturday looking for a win after consecutive league defeats. Forest’s expected goals total implies they should have scored but a flaw in their data shows a reason why. They also failed to find the net in a Carabao Cup home game with Leeds, meaning they have amassed 70 shots in all competitions without giving the home fans a goal to celebrate. As extreme as this situation has become, Forest scored only two goals more than the lowest home scorers in the Premier League last season (Burnley), drawing a blank on nine occasions. This is a longstanding issue. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

item.title: Uefa faces political flashpoint over Sevastopol’s ascent in Russian football
item.description: Promotion to third tier for Crimean club would be clear violation of governing body’s rules amid conflict in Ukraine Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier. Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
